title: Teaching Skills for New Teachers and Tutors
summary: Plan lessons, explain clearly, question well, assess and give feedback, manage a classroom and include every learner. For new teachers, tutors and trainers.
audience: New teachers, private tutors, trainers and student teachers

lessons.title: The teacher's role and how people learn

body.p: A teacher does more than give information. A good teacher plans, explains, questions, gives feedback, manages the room, and cares for the wellbeing of every learner. The goal is learning that lasts, not only covering the syllabus.

list: Learners build new understanding on what they already know, so find out their starting point first.
Attention is limited. Present a small amount at a time and check understanding before adding more.
Practice with feedback improves performance far more than listening alone.
Motivation grows when learners see purpose, experience success and feel respected.
Every class contains a range of ability, language, background and need.
Fairness and respect for all learners.
Safeguarding: protecting children from harm and following the school's reporting procedure.
Honesty about your own knowledge, and willingness to learn.
Confidentiality about learners' personal information.

body.tip: Observe a teacher you admire for a lesson and note what they do in the first five minutes, how they ask questions and how they end the lesson.

lessons.title: Planning a lesson with clear objectives

body.p: A lesson plan is a short route map for learning. Start from the end: what should learners be able to do by the end of the lesson? Write objectives with action verbs you can observe, such as define, calculate, compare, explain, solve or draw. 'Understand fractions' is vague. 'Add two fractions with different denominators and show the steps' can be checked.

steps: Starter (5 minutes): recall previous learning or spark curiosity with a question.
Teach (10 to 15 minutes): explain one idea with an example you work through aloud.
Guided practice (10 minutes): learners try similar problems while you circulate and help.
Independent practice (10 minutes): learners work alone on a task at the right level.
Check and close (5 minutes): quick questions or an exit ticket to see who has understood.

body.p: For a 45 minute lesson, the times above add up to 5 + 15 + 10 + 10 + 5 = 45. Plan a little slack, because activities nearly always take longer than expected.
Bloom's taxonomy lists levels from remembering and understanding to applying, analysing, evaluating and creating. A good lesson sequence moves learners up the levels, not only recall of facts.

body.tip: Prepare your examples and questions before the lesson. Improvising a worked example in front of a class is where many mistakes appear.

lessons.title: Explaining clearly and asking good questions

body.p: Clear explanations move from the known to the new, use plain words, give an example, and then a non-example so learners see the boundary of an idea. Draw or show where possible. Pause often and check understanding before continuing.

list: Ask the whole class, wait three to five seconds, then choose who answers. Waiting time improves the quality of answers.
Use open questions such as why, how and what if to promote thinking, and closed questions to check facts.
Ask learners to explain their reasoning even when the answer is right.
Respond to wrong answers with curiosity: what made you think that? Many wrong answers reveal a misconception you can fix.
Use mini whiteboards, show of hands, or paired talk so that every learner responds, not only the confident ones.

body.p: If learners are working in their second or third language, speak a little slower, use short sentences, write key words on the board and let them discuss first in their strongest language when appropriate.

Assessment gives information about learning. Formative assessment happens during learning so that teaching can change, such as quick questions, observation and short quizzes. Summative assessment happens at the end to record what has been achieved, such as an exam or final project.

list: Be specific: say what is correct, what is missing and what to do next.
Give feedback soon enough that learners can still act on it.
Focus on the work and the task, not on the learner's ability.
Give time in class to improve the work after feedback.

body.p: If 18 of 24 learners answer a question correctly, the percentage correct is 18 / 24 = 75%. If only 40% of learners get an item right, reteach the idea instead of moving on. Check which wrong option was chosen most often. It shows the common misconception.
Mark against clear criteria, give the same chance to everyone, record marks accurately and avoid letting a learner's behaviour in the past affect marking of the present work.

lessons.title: Classroom management and an inclusive classroom

body.p: Good behaviour comes from clear routines, high expectations and positive relationships, more than from punishment. Plan how learners enter, collect materials, ask for help and leave. Teach these routines like any other content.

list: Greet learners at the door and start work at once.
Give instructions one at a time and check that they were heard.
Praise the specific behaviour you want to see.
Move around the room so you can see all learners.
Deal with problems privately and calmly where you can, and be consistent.
Follow your school's policy for serious issues.

body.p: Inclusive teaching expects every learner to take part. Offer more than one way to access content (spoken, written, visual), allow different ways to show learning, and give extra support or challenge as needed. Learners with disabilities or learning difficulties, learners from poorer homes, girls and boys, and learners in a language that is not their home language all need your attention. Talk with parents and specialist staff if you have concerns about a learner.

body.tip: Seat learners who find it hard to concentrate near the front and next to a helpful peer, not at the back.

lessons.title: Growing as a teacher: reflection, planning your path and ethics

body.p: Teachers improve by reflecting on what happened. After each lesson, ask three questions: what did learners learn, how do I know, and what will I change next time? A short written note keeps these thoughts for next year.

list: Ask a colleague to observe a lesson and give feedback.
Observe other teachers.
Read about teaching practice, and test one idea at a time.
Join a professional community or association.
Keep a folder of resources, assessment items and what worked.

body.p: Routes to qualified teacher status differ by country and level. Many countries require a degree plus a teaching qualification and registration with a teaching council or ministry. Some also offer certificates for private tutors and early childhood educators. Check the rules where you want to work.

If you teach online or use technology, protect learners' data, keep communication with learners on official channels, and follow your school's safeguarding rules. Never share photos or personal details of learners without permission.

quiz.q: Which is a measurable lesson objective?
options: Add two fractions with different denominators and show the steps

quiz.q: Why should a teacher check learners' prior knowledge first?
options: New learning builds on what they already know

quiz.q: A lesson has starter 5, teach 15, guided practice 10, independent practice 10 and close 5 minutes. How long is it?
What is the purpose of wait time after asking a question?
options: To let more learners think and give better answers
A short quiz during a unit used to adjust teaching

quiz.q: 18 of 24 learners answer an item correctly. What percentage is that?
Which feedback is most useful to a learner?
options: Your method is right, but check the sign in step 3, then try the next two questions

quiz.q: What does a wrong answer often reveal?
options: A misconception that can be addressed

quiz.q: Which is a good start to classroom management?
options: Teach routines for entering, asking for help and leaving

quiz.q: What does inclusion mean in a classroom?
options: Putting struggling learners in a separate room
Making sure all learners can access and take part in learning

quiz.q: A teacher learns a child may be unsafe at home. What should she do first?
options: Follow the school's safeguarding procedure and report it to the designated person

quiz.q: After a lesson, which reflection is most useful?
options: What did learners learn, how do I know, and what will I change?
